title: In The Heat Of The Moment

sentences.en: From NPR, this is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是NPR，欢迎收听《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
Morgan Smalley has been performing with an improv comedy troupe since she was in college.
sentences.zh: 摩根·斯莫利从大学起就一直在参加即兴喜剧表演。

sentences.en: Look at me on page four.
But by now...
After dozens of performances, she's learned that you need more than a creative mind to get the audience laughing.
sentences.zh: 经过几十场演出，她明白了一个道理：想要观众发笑，光有创造力是不够的。

sentences.en: You also need to be a good listener.
sentences.zh: 你还得是个好的倾听者。

sentences.en: That means not just hearing what people say.
sentences.zh: 这意味着不仅仅是听别人说了什么。

sentences.en: You have to pick up on everything that surrounds the words.
sentences.zh: 你必须捕捉到言语之外的一切信息。

sentences.en: Like, let's say I came out, and instead of saying, happy birthday, like with a happy face, I could be like, happy birthday, and clearly that means that I'm upset.
sentences.zh: 比如，假设我走上台，没有面带微笑地说“生日快乐”，而是说“生日快乐”，那显然意味着我很生气。

sentences.en: And then we go from there, like, why am I mad at them?
sentences.zh: 然后我们再往下推，比如，我为什么生他们的气？

sentences.en: Is it that when it was my birthday last time, they treated me like garbage?
sentences.zh: 是因为上次我过生日时，他们把我当垃圾一样对待吗？

sentences.en: Things like that.
Morgan prides herself on being able to pick up on subtext, on being able to read between the lines, behind the lines.
sentences.zh: 摩根引以为傲的就是她能捕捉潜台词，能读懂字里行间，甚至字外之意。

sentences.en: When she does that well, she can hear the results immediately.
sentences.zh: 当她做得好时，她能立刻听到反馈。

sentences.en: When you get the laugh, it's just like such a self-esteem booSt.
sentences.zh: 当你逗笑观众时，那简直是对自尊心的一种极大提振。

sentences.en: It's like instant validation.
And instantly exhilarating.
sentences.zh: 而且瞬间让人兴奋不已。

sentences.en: That's how she felt at a recent show.
sentences.zh: 这就是她在最近一场演出中的感受。

sentences.en: There's one thing I did.
I was like a slug on stage.
sentences.zh: 我在台上像条鼻涕虫一样。

sentences.en: I, like, got on the floor and I, like, acted like a slug.
sentences.zh: 我趴在地上，像条鼻涕虫那样蠕动。

sentences.en: I inchwormed across the stage.
sentences.zh: 我像尺蠖一样在舞台上爬行。

sentences.en: Her fellow actors lit up.
sentences.zh: 她的搭档们都兴奋起来了。

sentences.en: The audience exploded in laughter.
When Morgan walked out of the theater that night, she was practically bursting.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上摩根走出剧院时，整个人几乎要飘起来了。

sentences.en: I just needed to do something with my energy.
sentences.zh: 我只是需要找个地方发泄一下精力。

sentences.en: Like, I didn't want to just go home and, like, go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不想就这样回家睡觉。

sentences.en: Just then...
This guy, like, walked out of nowhere.
sentences.zh: 有个家伙不知从哪儿冒了出来。

sentences.en: He was carrying a tripod and a bunch of other stuff.
sentences.zh: 他扛着一个三脚架和一堆乱七八糟的东西。

sentences.en: Like a sack with stuff in it.
sentences.zh: 就像一个装满杂物的袋子。

sentences.en: And he was just like, does anybody want to buy this tripod?
sentences.zh: 他直接问：“有人想买这个三脚架吗？”

sentences.en: And I was like, yeah, I want to buy this tripod.
sentences.zh: 我当时就说：“好啊，我想买这个三脚架。”

sentences.en: I think I could get a lot of you set of a tripod.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这三脚架我能派上大用场。

sentences.en: I was like, how much?
And he said, $25.
And also, I'm going to give you this $50 Amazon gift card.
sentences.zh: “而且，我还要送你这张50美元的亚马逊礼品卡。”

sentences.en: And I was like, okay, a tripod and a $50 Amazon gift card for $25.
sentences.zh: 我心想，好吧，25美元就能买个三脚架和一张50美元的亚马逊礼品卡。

sentences.en: Wow, this guy is so cool.
I'm totally going to do that.
The high she felt from inchworming across the stage just got even higher.
sentences.zh: 她在舞台上蠕动带来的兴奋感，此刻更上一层楼了。

sentences.en: Morgan walked with a guy to an ATM.
sentences.zh: 摩根陪那个人去了一趟自动取款机。

sentences.en: I got my money in 20s.
sentences.zh: 我取出来的钱都是20美元面值的。

sentences.en: So I had to either give him $20 or $40.
sentences.zh: 所以我只能给他20美元或者40美元。

sentences.en: She asked if she could give him $20 rather than the full $25.
sentences.zh: 她问能不能只给他20美元，而不是全额的25美元。

sentences.en: He was like, you give me whatever you want to give me.
sentences.zh: 他说：“你想给多少就给多少。”

sentences.en: And I was like, you're so cool.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，你真是太酷了。

sentences.en: I'm going to give you $40.
And I gave him $40.
And then he gave me, like, a shoebox full of other random things.
sentences.zh: 然后他给了我一个装满各种杂物的鞋盒。

sentences.en: And I was like, he's so cool.
Morgan felt like she had hit the jackpot.
sentences.zh: 摩根觉得自己中了大奖。

sentences.en: There was a loofah in there.
There was a bunch of pens.
And I got really excited about the pens because, I don't know, I just love pens.
sentences.zh: 我对那些笔感到非常兴奋，因为我也不知道为什么，我就是喜欢笔。

sentences.en: There's like stress balls in there.
There was like a diamond cleaner.
I've never heard of a diamond cleaner before, but it's got like bristles at the end and like this juice on the inside.
sentences.zh: 我以前从没听说过钻石清洁剂，但它末端有刷毛，里面还有液体。

sentences.en: What else is in there?
I had some craft supplies.
And he also threw in a pair of women's shoes.
sentences.zh: 他还顺手塞进了一双女鞋。

sentences.en: They weren't my size, but I was like, I can sell those.
sentences.zh: 虽然尺码不对，但我当时想，我可以把它们卖掉。

sentences.en: This is awesome.
Morgan couldn't wait to show her roommates the loot.
sentences.zh: 摩根迫不及待地想向室友展示她的战利品。

sentences.en: She burst into her apartment and told them about her unbelievable good fortune.
sentences.zh: 她冲进公寓，告诉她们自己好运得不可思议。

sentences.en: They were like, what is wrong with you?
sentences.zh: 她们却说：“你脑子没毛病吧？”

sentences.en: They were like, okay, what this guy did is he took the stuff out of cars that weren't locked and then he sold it to you for money.
sentences.zh: 她们说：“听着，这家伙做的事就是从没锁的车里偷东西，然后卖给你换钱。”

sentences.en: I was like, no, no, he was so cool.
No, he was so nice.
He said he was moving.
He was getting rid of the shoes.
He said they were his girlfriend's shoes.
sentences.zh: 他说那是他女朋友的鞋。

sentences.en: He said he was distancing himself from technology.
sentences.zh: 他说他想远离科技产品。

sentences.en: That's why he couldn't use the gift card.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他不能用那张礼品卡。

sentences.en: And he said his aunt gave him that gift card and that's why he didn't want it.
sentences.zh: 他还说那张礼品卡是他阿姨给他的，所以他才不想要。

sentences.en: And slowly, like, my universe just, like, unraveled.
sentences.zh: 然后，我的世界观慢慢地……崩塌了。

sentences.en: And I was like, no, I just bought a bunch of stolen stuff.
sentences.zh: 我心想，不，我只是买了一堆赃物。

sentences.en: Why did Morgan, who prides herself on being able to read subtext and situations, fail to see what seemed obvious to her friends?
sentences.zh: 为什么以擅长解读潜台词和局势自居的摩根，却没能看出朋友们一眼就看穿的事实呢？

sentences.en: I like to think of myself as, like, a pretty logical person.
sentences.zh: 我一直认为自己是个挺理性的人。

sentences.en: But in that moment, I didn't have any logic.
sentences.zh: 但在那一刻，我完全失去了逻辑。

sentences.en: Like, I wasn't questioning the situation.
sentences.zh: 我根本没有质疑那个情况。

sentences.en: I was just being super impulsive.
And so, yeah, in that way, I think I was being a pretty different person.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，在那方面，我觉得自己变成了一个完全不同的人。

sentences.en: It's as if there are two people within Morgan and neither understands the other.
sentences.zh: 就好像摩根体内住着两个人，而且谁也不理解谁。

sentences.en: Logical Morgan thinks impulsive Morgan made a glaring mistake.
sentences.zh: 理性的摩根认为冲动的摩根犯了一个明显的错误。

sentences.en: But impulsive Morgan is just as bewildered by logical Morgan.
sentences.zh: 但冲动的摩根对理性的摩根也同样感到困惑。

sentences.en: Who would pass up a deal like this?
sentences.zh: 谁会放过这样的便宜呢？

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, we explore how certain situations
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，我们将探讨某些情境如何

sentences.en: cause us to become strangers to ourselves.
sentences.zh: 让我们变得连自己都不认识自己。

sentences.en: I definitely didn't maintain cool and calm.
My entire body froze.
I was just an absolute blubbering mess.
sentences.zh: 我当时完全乱了阵脚，只会哭闹。

sentences.en: I became filled with anger.
And I just kind of lost it.
And we look at the deep psychological mystery that occurs during these moments.
sentences.zh: 我们将审视这些时刻背后深层的心理奥秘。

sentences.en: No matter how many times we discover the strangers living inside us,
sentences.zh: 无论我们多少次发现内心住着一个陌生人，

sentences.en: the next time always catches us by surprise.
sentences.zh: 下一次遇到时，我们依然会感到措手不及。

sentences.en: Quick heads up, this episode contains stories about sex, sex work, and sexual harassment.
sentences.zh: 温馨提示，本期节目包含关于性、性工作和性骚扰的内容。

sentences.en: The Pittsburgh area is home to some of the steepest hills in America.
sentences.zh: 匹兹堡地区拥有美国一些最陡峭的山坡。

sentences.en: George Lowenstein used to run these hills every week with his friend Jules.
sentences.zh: 乔治·洛温斯坦过去每周都会和他的朋友朱尔斯一起跑这些山坡。

sentences.en: We would leave our offices and run down through the park all the way down to the river.
sentences.zh: 我们会离开办公室，穿过公园，一路跑到河边。

sentences.en: And then there is a town called Greenfield with a very, very big hill.
sentences.zh: 然后有一个叫格林菲尔德的小镇，那里有一座非常非常大的山坡。

sentences.en: It's so steep that stairs are built into the hill to make it easier to climb.
sentences.zh: 它陡峭到为了方便攀爬，山坡上专门修了台阶。

sentences.en: We would get absolutely exhausted on the way up.
sentences.zh: 我们在爬上去的时候总是精疲力竭。

sentences.en: And we'd kind of be egging one another on and be feeling very, very miserable.
sentences.zh: 我们会互相怂恿，感觉非常非常痛苦。

sentences.en: On the way up to the peak, all he could think of was the pain.
sentences.zh: 在爬向顶峰的过程中，他满脑子想的都是痛苦。

sentences.en: But moments later?
It was all forgotten within maybe 10, 20 seconds.
sentences.zh: 可能也就10到20秒，一切就都忘了。

sentences.en: The more George thought about it, the more it seemed like a puzzle.
sentences.zh: 乔治越想越觉得这像个谜题。

sentences.en: As he was climbing the hill, the idea of relief was inconceivable.
sentences.zh: 当他在爬坡时，解脱的想法简直不可想象。

sentences.en: The pain felt endless.
sentences.zh: 那种痛苦感觉永无止境。

sentences.en: But the moment he crested the hill, the pain faded so quickly that in his memory, it hadn't been so bad.
sentences.zh: 但当他登上坡顶的那一刻，痛苦消散得如此之快，以至于在他的记忆里，那并没有那么糟糕。

sentences.en: A few days later, he would lace up his shoes and go running with Jules again.
sentences.zh: 几天后，他会再次系好鞋带，和朱尔斯一起去跑步。

sentences.en: It occurred to George that this gap in perception was psychologically important
sentences.zh: 乔治意识到这种感知上的差距在心理学上很重要，

sentences.en: and applied to more than just the pain of running.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅适用于跑步带来的痛苦。

sentences.en: I realized that when you're not in pain or cold or experiencing a powerful emotion like anger or fear,
sentences.zh: 我意识到，当你没有处于痛苦、寒冷，或者没有经历愤怒、恐惧等强烈情绪时，

sentences.en: it's very difficult to imagine yourself in that situation.
sentences.zh: 你很难想象自己身处那种情境下的感受。

sentences.en: There is a reason this happens.
Emotions completely transform us as people.
sentences.zh: 情绪会彻底改变我们这个人。

sentences.en: So when we're in one emotional state, it's as if we're a different person than we are when we're in a different emotional state.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们处于某种情绪状态时，就好像我们变成了与另一种情绪状态下完全不同的人。

sentences.en: George has thought about this phenomenon a lot.
sentences.zh: 乔治对这种现象思考了很多。

sentences.en: As a professor of psychology and economics at Carnegie Mellon University,
sentences.zh: 作为卡内基梅隆大学的心理学和经济学教授，

sentences.en: he has conducted dozens of studies to understand how our emotional states affect us.
sentences.zh: 他进行了几十项研究，以了解我们的情绪状态如何影响我们。

sentences.en: One of his earliest studies involved ice water.
sentences.zh: 他最早的研究之一涉及冰水。

sentences.en: My colleague wanted to be the guinea pig for the studies and you're supposed to put your hand in the cold water for like a minute.
sentences.zh: 我的同事想当研究的实验品，你需要把手放在冷水里大约一分钟。

sentences.en: He put his hand in the cold water and 20 seconds later, he pulled it out.
sentences.zh: 他把手放进冷水里，20秒后就抽了出来。

sentences.en: And then a minute later, he said, that's ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 一分钟后，他说：“这太荒谬了。”

sentences.en: I can do it because he couldn't remember the pain anymore.
sentences.zh: “我能做到。”因为他已经记不起那种痛苦了。

sentences.en: Expecting fully that he would be able to sustain the minute in the cold water.
sentences.zh: 他完全相信自己能坚持在冷水里待上一分钟。

sentences.en: And then about 20 seconds later, he pulled his hand out again.
sentences.zh: 结果大约20秒后，他又把手抽了出来。

sentences.en: It was just like what George experienced on his runs.
sentences.zh: 这和乔治在跑步时的经历如出一辙。

sentences.en: As soon as his colleague pulled his hand out of the freezing water, it was like he was struck with amnesia.
sentences.zh: 当他的同事把手从冰冷的水中抽出来时，就像患了失忆症一样。

sentences.en: George came up with a name for what was happening.
sentences.zh: 乔治为这种现象起了一个名字。

sentences.en: The hot, cold empathy gap.
Usually, when we think about empathy, we think about how we relate to other people.
sentences.zh: 通常当我们想到同理心时，我们想到的是我们如何与他人产生共鸣。

sentences.en: George's insight is that we regularly lack empathy for ourselves when we are in a different emotional state.
sentences.zh: 乔治的见解是，当我们处于不同的情绪状态时，我们经常对自己缺乏同理心。

sentences.en: When we're angry, we can't imagine being calm.
sentences.zh: 当我们愤怒时，我们无法想象自己冷静的样子。

sentences.en: When we are tranquil, it's hard to imagine being so angry that we could hurt someone.
sentences.zh: 当我们平静时，很难想象自己会愤怒到伤害别人。

sentences.en: The hot, cold empathy gap can also be caused by physiological states.
sentences.zh: “热-冷同理心差距”也可能由生理状态引起。

sentences.en: When we are really hungry, all our resolutions about healthy eating evaporate.
sentences.zh: 当我们非常饿的时候，所有关于健康饮食的决心都会烟消云散。

sentences.en: When we are full, it's easy to forget what it felt like to be hungry.
sentences.zh: 当我们吃饱时，很容易忘记饥饿时的感觉。

sentences.en: We imagine that we will stick to salads the next time.
sentences.zh: 我们想象下次一定会坚持吃沙拉。

sentences.en: The hot and cold in the hot, cold empathy gap are a shorthand.
sentences.zh: “热-冷同理心差距”中的“热”和“冷”是一种速记法。

sentences.en: They describe strong emotional and physiological states.
sentences.zh: 它们描述了强烈的情绪和生理状态。

sentences.en: When we're in a cold state, we're logical, deliberate.
sentences.zh: 当我们处于“冷”状态时，我们是理性的、深思熟虑的。

sentences.en: When we're in a hot state, our emotions overtake us.
sentences.zh: 当我们处于“热”状态时，情绪就会占据上风。

sentences.en: Morgan Smalley was in a hot state when a young man sold her a sack of random stuff.
sentences.zh: 摩根·斯莫利在那个年轻人向她兜售一袋杂物时，就处于一种“热”状态。

sentences.en: In her excitement, her skepticism failed to kick in.
sentences.zh: 在兴奋之中，她的怀疑心理没能发挥作用。

sentences.en: Another familiar hot state?
sentences.zh: 还有什么常见的“热”状态吗？

sentences.en: Sexual arousal.
Can I talk about that on NPR?
sentences.zh: 我能在 NPR（美国国家公共电台）上谈论这个吗？

sentences.en: Like, I don't know.
The answer is yes.
So parents of young children, here's your warning.
sentences.zh: 所以，各位家长，这是给你们的提醒。

sentences.en: When Irene Pemberton was in middle school, she devoted as much time to sex ed as her classmates may have spent hanging out at the mall.
sentences.zh: 艾琳·彭伯顿（Irene Pemberton）上初中时，她花在性教育上的时间，可能和同学们在商场闲逛的时间一样多。

sentences.en: Every Sunday evening for about a year, her parents drove her to a Unitarian church for a two-hour session.
sentences.zh: 大约一年里，每个周日晚上，她父母都会开车送她去一家一神论派教堂，参加两小时的课程。

sentences.en: We learned everything, you know.
sentences.zh: 我们学到了所有东西，你知道的。

sentences.en: Like, they had, like, the condoms, you know, putting on bananas kind of deal.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们会教那种，你知道的，在香蕉上练习戴避孕套之类的东西。

sentences.en: Irene's family also spoke frankly about sex, like the time in high school when Irene got an IUD and had a conversation about it with her mom.
sentences.zh: 艾琳的家人也坦诚地谈论性，比如高中时，艾琳装了宫内节育器（IUD），并和她妈妈聊过这件事。

sentences.en: I just remember her saying that I still have to use condoms and, you know, to still be careful.
sentences.zh: 我只记得她说我仍然必须使用避孕套，而且，你知道的，还是要小心。

sentences.en: In other words, Irene received an unusually candid, comprehensive sex education.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，艾琳接受了异常坦诚且全面的性教育。

sentences.en: All those hours sitting on church couches and talking to her family made her confident that she'd make good decisions when it came to sex.
sentences.zh: 在教堂沙发上坐着的那无数个小时，以及与家人的交谈，让她确信自己在面对性时能做出正确的决定。

sentences.en: I was like, well, obviously.
Obviously, I would use condoms, like, if I didn't, like, know the person very well and, like, we're not monogamous or anything.
sentences.zh: 很明显，我会使用避孕套，比如，如果我不太了解对方，而且，我们又不是一夫一妻制之类的。

sentences.en: And I probably was like, I would do it every time.
sentences.zh: 而且我当时可能想的是，我每次都会这么做。

sentences.en: And she did.
That is, until she met one special suitor.
sentences.zh: 直到她遇到了一个特别的追求者。

sentences.en: He's just kind of like a greasy guy that, like, wears, like, overalls with no underwear.
sentences.zh: 他就是那种油腻腻的家伙，比如，穿着那种连体工装裤，里面还不穿内裤。

sentences.en: And, like, so I think it was cool.
sentences.zh: 而且，所以我觉得这挺酷的。

sentences.en: I thought I was pretty charmed by that.
Wait, how did you know that he wears overalls with no underwear?
sentences.zh: 等等，你怎么知道他穿连体工装裤还不穿内裤？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
That was later.
That's my take on him now.

sentences.zh: 但她唯一记得的是，她坚持完成了整个轮班。

sentences.en: I asked her why she felt compelled to stay when she herself would have predicted she would do otherwise.
sentences.zh: 我问她，当她自己本会预测自己会采取不同做法时，为什么会感到不得不留下来。

sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种非常普遍的反应，人们会说，是的，我坚持下去了，因为显然我应该在开始时多问一些，但我没有。

sentences.en: This is psychologist Julie Woodzica.
sentences.zh: 这是心理学家朱莉·伍兹卡。

sentences.en: I am a professor at Washington and Lee University.
sentences.zh: 我是华盛顿与李大学的一名教授。

sentences.en: Julie has spent years studying how people react in situations like the one Nina found herself in.
sentences.zh: 朱莉多年来一直在研究人们在妮娜所处的那种情况下会有什么反应。

sentences.en: Many of these people asked themselves the same questions.
sentences.zh: 许多这样的人都问过自己同样的问题。

sentences.en: Why didn't I speak up?
Why didn't I protest?
Why did I go through with it?
sentences.zh: 为什么我坚持做下去了？

sentences.en: Some of Julie's earliest thoughts on sexual harassment and abuse came together when she was a college student.
sentences.zh: 朱莉关于性骚扰和虐待的一些最早的想法是在她还是大学生时形成的。

sentences.en: Like millions of others, she witnessed the tectonic event in 1991 that brought the term sexual harassment into popular use.
sentences.zh: 像数以百万计的其他人一样，她目睹了1991年那场将“性骚扰”一词推向大众视野的标志性事件。

sentences.en: It was a Senate testimony of law professor Anita Hill.
sentences.zh: 那是法学教授安妮塔·希尔的参议院证词。

sentences.en: She claimed Supreme Court nominee Clarence Thomas had sexually harassed her while he was her supervisor.
sentences.zh: 她声称最高法院提名人克拉伦斯·托马斯在她担任其下属时曾对她进行性骚扰。

sentences.en: After a brief discussion of work, he would turn the conversation to a discussion of sexual matters.
sentences.zh: 在简短的工作讨论之后，他会把谈话转向性话题。

sentences.en: Before an all-male judiciary committee, she alleged he had made sexual advances and told explicit jokes.
sentences.zh: 在全男性的司法委员会面前，她指控他曾进行性挑逗并讲过露骨的笑话。

sentences.en: He commented on what I was wearing in terms of whether it made me more or less sexually attractive.
sentences.zh: 他评论我的穿着，看它是否让我更有或更少性吸引力。

sentences.en: He talked about pornographic materials.
On several occasions, Thomas told me graphically of his own sexual prowess.
sentences.zh: 托马斯曾多次向我生动地描述他自己的性能力。

sentences.en: The nation was wrapped and divided.
sentences.zh: 全国都陷入了震惊和分裂。

sentences.en: I remember really, really vividly people saying, like, no, she's lying.
sentences.zh: 我记得非常非常清楚，人们说，不，她在撒谎。

sentences.en: She's got to be lying.
There was one specific detail that led many people to that conclusion.
sentences.zh: 有一个具体的细节导致许多人得出了那个结论。

sentences.en: After Anita Hill allegedly experienced harassment, she was given an opportunity to work for Clarence Thomas again.
sentences.zh: 在安妮塔·希尔据称遭受骚扰后，她又获得了为克拉伦斯·托马斯工作的机会。

sentences.en: She took it.
During the hearings, Senator Alan Simpson pressed her on this point.
sentences.zh: 在听证会上，参议员艾伦·辛普森就这一点向她施压。

sentences.en: If what you say this man said to you, occurred,
sentences.zh: 如果这个男人对你所说的话确实发生了，

sentences.en: why in God's name, when he left his position of power or status or authority over you,
sentences.zh: 为什么看在上帝的份上，当他不再拥有对你的权力、地位或权威时，

sentences.en: and you left it in 1983,
sentences.zh: 而你在1983年离开了那个职位，

sentences.en: why in God's name would you ever speak to a man like that the rest of your life?
sentences.zh: 为什么看在上帝的份上，你余生还会和那样的男人说话？

sentences.en: That's a very good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: And I'm sure that I can't not answer that to your satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 我相信我无法给出让你满意的答案。

sentences.en: That is one of the things that I have tried to do today.
sentences.zh: 那是我今天试图做的事情之一。

sentences.en: I have suggested that I was afraid of retaliation.
I was afraid of damage to my professional life.
sentences.zh: 我害怕我的职业生涯受到损害。

sentences.en: And I believe that you have to understand that this response,
sentences.zh: 我相信你必须理解这种反应，

sentences.en: and that's one of the things that I have come to understand about harassment,
sentences.zh: 这也是我开始理解关于骚扰的事情之一，

sentences.en: that this response, this kind of response, is not atypical.
sentences.zh: 这种反应，这种类型的反应，并非不典型。

sentences.en: And I can't explain.
It takes an expert in psychology to explain how that can happen.
sentences.zh: 这需要心理学专家来解释这种情况是如何发生的。

sentences.en: But it can happen, because it happened to me.
sentences.zh: 但它确实会发生，因为它发生在我身上。

sentences.en: By the early 2000s, Julie had become one of those experts in psychology.
sentences.zh: 到21世纪初，朱莉已经成为了那些心理学专家之一。

sentences.en: She and her collaborator, Marianne LaFrance,
sentences.zh: 她和她的合作者玛丽安·拉弗朗斯，

sentences.en: found themselves talking about how people reacted to Anita Hill's testimony.
sentences.zh: 发现她们在讨论人们对安妮塔·希尔证词的反应。

sentences.en: We noticed a lot of people said,
I never would have responded that way if I had been sexually harassed.
sentences.zh: 如果我受到性骚扰，我绝不会那样回应。

sentences.en: I would have told them to stop.
And I probably would have left the job.
I definitely would have followed him to another job.
sentences.zh: 我绝对会跟着他去另一份工作。

sentences.en: Julie realized some of the most important questions about sexual harassment
sentences.zh: 朱莉意识到关于性骚扰的一些最重要的问题

sentences.en: had not been studied at all.
There was a lot on how women remembered responding,
sentences.zh: 关于女性如何回忆自己的反应有很多研究，

sentences.en: and there was a good amount on how they anticipated they would respond.
sentences.zh: 关于她们预想自己会如何反应也有相当多的研究。

sentences.en: But there was nothing at that point on looking at how women actually responded.
sentences.zh: 但在那时，对于女性实际上是如何反应的，却没有任何研究。

sentences.en: Julie set out to understand how women react to sexual harassment as it's happening.
sentences.zh: 朱莉着手研究女性在遭遇性骚扰时会有何反应。

sentences.en: In the first phase of the study,
we had roughly 200 women come into the lab,
sentences.zh: 我们让大约200名女性来到实验室，

sentences.en: and we gave them a scenario that they needed to read through.
sentences.zh: 并给她们提供了一个需要阅读的情境。

sentences.en: Here's the scenario.
You're interviewing for a job as a research assistant.
sentences.zh: 你正在面试一份研究助理的工作。

sentences.en: The interviewer is in his mid-30s.
sentences.zh: 面试官是一名30多岁的男性。

sentences.en: You're in an office alone with him.
sentences.zh: 你和他单独待在一间办公室里。

sentences.en: And, you know, after initial greeting, he starts asking you some questions.
sentences.zh: 寒暄过后，他开始问你一些问题。

sentences.en: They're standard interview questions.
sentences.zh: 这些都是标准的面试问题。

sentences.en: Until this one.
Do you have a boyfriend?
A few questions later.
Do people find you desirable?
sentences.zh: 人们觉得你有吸引力吗？

sentences.en: The interview continues.
Then he asks,
Do you think it's important for women to wear bras to work?
sentences.zh: 你认为女性上班穿胸罩重要吗？

sentences.en: Remember, this is a job interview.
sentences.zh: 记住，这是一场求职面试。

sentences.en: The women who participated in Julie's study imagined the situation
sentences.zh: 参与朱莉研究的女性设想了这种情况，

sentences.en: and were asked to describe how they thought they'd react.
sentences.zh: 并被要求描述她们认为自己会作何反应。

sentences.en: The response was overwhelming.
About 90% of the women thought that they would respond in a very assertive and sometimes aggressive way.
sentences.zh: 约90%的女性认为她们会以非常坚定、有时甚至是激进的方式做出回应。

sentences.en: So about 60% said that they would confront assertively, that they would say to him,
sentences.zh: 约60%的人表示她们会坚定地对抗，她们会对他直说：

sentences.en: that's inappropriate, you shouldn't ask those questions.
sentences.zh: 这很不妥，你不应该问这些问题。

sentences.en: About 30% said that they would leave the interview or that they would often say,
sentences.zh: 约30%的人表示她们会离开面试现场，或者她们常说：

sentences.en: I'd tell him off or I'd slap him and then leave.
sentences.zh: 我会训斥他，或者我会扇他一巴掌然后离开。

sentences.en: Besides confronting the interviewer and leaving the interview,
sentences.zh: 除了对抗面试官和离开面试现场外，

sentences.en: many participants said they'd do something else.
sentences.zh: 许多参与者表示她们还会做其他事情。

sentences.en: 68% of all respondents said that they would refuse to answer at least one of those three questions.
sentences.zh: 68%的受访者表示，她们会拒绝回答那三个问题中的至少一个。

sentences.en: The women were not only asked to predict what they'd do,
sentences.zh: 这些女性不仅被要求预测她们会怎么做，

sentences.en: but to describe the emotion they would feel.
sentences.zh: 还要描述她们会感受到的情绪。

sentences.en: A lot of women, about 30%, said that they would feel anger.
sentences.zh: 很多女性，约30%，表示她们会感到愤怒。

sentences.en: Women who predicted they'd be angry were more likely to say they'd confront the interviewer.
sentences.zh: 预测自己会感到愤怒的女性，更有可能表示她们会对抗面试官。

sentences.en: Anger was galvanizing.
We were interested in fear, too.
How many people thought they'd be a little bit afraid?
sentences.zh: 有多少人认为自己会感到一点害怕？

sentences.en: And only 2% of people said that they would be afraid.
sentences.zh: 只有2%的人表示她们会感到害怕。

sentences.en: And fear was not correlated with confronting.
sentences.zh: 而且恐惧与对抗行为之间没有关联。

sentences.en: So this doesn't sound like Nina Fuller at all.
sentences.zh: 所以这听起来一点也不像妮娜·富勒的情况。

sentences.en: These women were all assertive, angry, indignant.
sentences.zh: 这些女性都很坚定、愤怒、愤慨。

sentences.en: They were sure they would tell the man off.
sentences.zh: 她们确信自己会训斥那个男人。

sentences.en: In the second part of the study,
Julie set up an experiment to test whether women actually did what they forecast they would do.
sentences.zh: 朱莉设计了一个实验，来测试女性是否真的会做她们预想中会做的事。

sentences.en: We had 50 women who were applying for a job.
sentences.zh: 我们找了50名正在申请工作的女性。

sentences.en: The job was a research assistant in a lab.
sentences.zh: 这份工作是实验室的研究助理。

sentences.en: The women would come into the interview, and we had covert cameras set up.
sentences.zh: 女性们来到面试现场，我们安装了隐蔽摄像头。

sentences.en: Their interviewer was a man in his mid-30s.
sentences.zh: 面试官是一名30多岁的男性。

sentences.en: He asked those three questions.
The same three questions from the first phase of the study.
sentences.zh: 与研究第一阶段完全相同的那三个问题。

sentences.en: Do you have a boyfriend?
Do people find you desirable?
sentences.zh: 人们觉得你有吸引力吗？

sentences.en: Do you think it's important for women to wear bras to work?
sentences.zh: 你认为女性上班穿胸罩重要吗？

sentences.en: What was different here was that the women weren't imagining a job interview.
sentences.zh: 这里的不同之处在于，这些女性并不是在想象一场面试。

sentences.en: They were in a job interview, or so they believed.
sentences.zh: 她们确实身处面试之中，或者说她们是这么认为的。

sentences.en: So how did they react?
sentences.zh: 那么她们是如何反应的呢？

sentences.en: Did 90% respond assertively?
sentences.zh: 有90%的人坚定地回应了吗？

sentences.en: Tell the interviewer off?
Slap him and walk out?
sentences.zh: 扇了他一巴掌然后走人了吗？

sentences.en: Nobody left.
Every single person answered every single question.
sentences.zh: 每个人都回答了每一个问题。

sentences.en: Some women did speak up, but generally not until the end of the interview.
sentences.zh: 有些女性确实开口了，但通常要等到面试快结束时才说。

sentences.en: 36% of the participants at that point said very politely,
sentences.zh: 当时有36%的参与者非常礼貌地说：

sentences.en: Yeah, I was just wondering, you know, why did you ask about me being desirable?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我只是想知道，你为什么要问我是否有吸引力？

sentences.en: There was another important difference between the women's responses in the two parts of the study.
sentences.zh: 女性在研究两部分中的反应还有另一个重要的区别。

sentences.en: So you remember in the anticipated study, most women responded that they'd be angry, very few fearful.
sentences.zh: 还记得在预想研究中，大多数女性回答说她们会感到愤怒，很少有人感到害怕。

sentences.en: And it was the flip in this study.
sentences.zh: 但在这次研究中情况完全反过来了。

sentences.en: So we found that many women reported feeling afraid in that situation, and anger was not very much reported.
sentences.zh: 我们发现许多女性报告说在这种情况下感到害怕，而感到愤怒的报告则很少。

sentences.en: While the women who imagined being sexually harassed thought they'd be angry and that anger would propel them to act,
sentences.zh: 虽然那些想象自己被性骚扰的女性认为她们会感到愤怒，并且愤怒会促使她们采取行动，

sentences.en: women who were face-to-face with a harasser, in fact, experienced fear.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，与骚扰者面对面的女性却体验到了恐惧。

sentences.en: There's clearly an aspect of the study that should make you uneasy.
sentences.zh: 这项研究显然有一个方面会让你感到不安。

sentences.en: Researchers brought in unsuspecting women for what they thought were job interviews
sentences.zh: 研究人员把毫无防备的女性带到她们以为是求职面试的地方，

sentences.en: and then subjected them to harassment to see how they would behave.
sentences.zh: 然后让她们遭受骚扰，以观察她们的行为。
